slides.title: Beyond Heuristics: A Standardized Real2Sim Pipeline for Physical Human Robot Interaction in Human-in-the-Loop Simulation
slides.tldr: REAL2SIM PIPELINE FOR PHYSICAL HUMAN-ROBOT INTERACTION
slides.highlight: This research introduces a Real2Sim pipeline to identify physical human-robot interaction dynamics, improving the fidelity of Human-in-the-Loop simulations for assistive robots. It is relevant to RwB for its focus on embodied human-robot interaction and the use of Human Digital Twins for personalized controller verification.

card.one_liner: A standardized Real2Sim pipeline for identifying coupled physical human-robot interaction dynamics to improve HITL simulation fidelity.
card.key_idea: A 6-DoF viscoelastic model is calibrated using CMA-ES and a 'Safe & Comfortable' operating point, with ICC analysis separating shareable from subject-specific parameters.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 6 subjects using LOSO protocol, postural sway (RMSE, anisotropy), and gait kinematics (RoM, Pearson r) against isotropic baselines.
card.limitation: The small cohort size (N=5 for calibration) prevents regressing uncertain parameters on anthropometric data like waist or mass.

slides.title: SoftVTBench: A Safety-Aware Visuo-Tactile Benchmark for Physically Constrained Robotic Manipulation of Deformable Objects
slides.tldr: NEW SAFETY-AWARE VISUO-TACTILE BENCHMARK FOR DEFORMABLE OBJECTS
slides.highlight: SoftVTBench introduces a benchmark that evaluates both goal success and physical safety in deformable object manipulation, demonstrating that tactile sensing improves safety and reduces object deformation.

card.one_liner: A visuo-tactile benchmark for deformable object manipulation evaluating both task completion and physical interaction safety.
card.key_idea: Uses FEM-simulated objects in Isaac Sim to measure 'Safety Success' (no drops and deformation below thresholds) alongside standard 'Goal Success'.
card.evaluation: Evaluated $\pi_{0.5}$ baselines across four task suites; results show tactile sensing improves Safety Success (e.g., 21.4% to 35.6% on object-centric tasks).
card.limitation: Limited set of assets and task variations; simulation may not fully capture real-world soft-body dynamics.

slides.title: Feeling the Unexpected: ResTacVLA for Contact-Rich Manipulation via Residual Tactile Representation
slides.tldr: RESIDUAL TACTILE REPRESENTATION FOR VLA MODELS
slides.highlight: ResTacVLA addresses modality collapse in vision-language-action models by using residual tactile representations to prioritize surprising physical stimuli over predictable visual cues.

card.one_liner: ResTacVLA improves contact-rich manipulation by integrating tactile feedback as a residual of visual predictions.
card.key_idea: A Cross-Modal Predictor extracts tactile residuals (surprises) relative to visual priors, discretizing them into VQ Latent Contact Primitives and adaptively gating them via a Surprise-Aware Gate.
card.evaluation: Tested on five real-world tasks (e.g., screwing, insertion) against VLA baselines; achieved 62.8% average success, significantly outperforming vision-only and naive fusion models.

slides.title: TACO: TActile World Model as a Self-COrrector for Scalable VLA Post-Training
slides.tldr: TACTILE-AWARE WORLD MODEL FOR VLA POST-TRAINING
slides.highlight: TACO introduces a tactile-aware world model that converts real-world failures into imagined visuo-tactile corrections to improve VLA model performance in contact-rich manipulation.

card.one_liner: TACO uses a tactile-aware world model to synthesize corrective visuo-tactile data for VLA post-training.
card.key_idea: A Recognize–Imagine–Label loop identifies failure states, imagines visuo-tactile corrections via joint video-force denoising, and uses knowledge-insulated adaptation to update the VLA without eroding visual priors.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on six real-world contact-rich tasks; achieved 44% absolute success rate improvement over the base policy across two iterations.
card.limitation: Imagined corrections are generated offline rather than online during deployment.

slides.title: VT-WAM: Visual-Tactile World Action Model for Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.tldr: VISUAL-TACTILE WORLD ACTION MODEL FOR CONTACT-RICH MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: VT-WAM introduces a unified flow matching framework that jointly predicts future visual states, tactile deformation, and actions to improve contact-rich manipulation.

card.one_liner: VT-WAM improves contact-rich manipulation by jointly predicting future visual, tactile, and action dynamics.
card.key_idea: A flow-matching framework using Asymmetric MoT Attention to bridge visual anchors with tactile sequences and AVTAG to prioritize tactile evidence during contact phases.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on six real-world tasks; achieved 71.67% average success rate, significantly outperforming Fast-WAM (45.00%) and OmniVTLA (35.83%).
card.limitation: The current work focuses on individual-task specialization; multi-task training and scaling laws remain unexplored.

slides.title: Closing the Reality Gap: Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Deployment for Dexterous Force-Based Grasping and Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates zero-shot sim-to-real transfer for dexterous hands using tactile feedback and joint torque sensing. It is relevant to MOSAIC's focus on physics/force-based skill acquisition and the regulation of physical interactions.

card.one_liner: Achieves zero-shot sim-to-real transfer for force-controllable grasping and in-hand manipulation using dense tactile and torque feedback.
card.key_idea: Combines a fast distance-field tactile simulator, current-to-torque calibration, and randomized actuator dynamics modeling within an asymmetric actor-critic PPO pipeline.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a 12-DoF XHand via force-tracking and object rotation; ablation studies show 6D orientation and tactile feedback are critical for success.

slides.title: OmniTacTune: Policy-Agnostic Real-World RL for Tactile Residual Adaptation of Visual Policies
slides.tldr: TACTILE RESIDUAL ADAPTATION FOR VISUAL POLICIES
slides.highlight: OmniTacTune introduces a policy-agnostic RL pipeline that uses tactile feedback to correct pretrained visual policies in contact-rich manipulation tasks. It demonstrates significant success rate improvements across diverse tasks with efficient online interaction.

card.one_liner: OmniTacTune adapts tactile feedback to pretrained visual policies via a two-stage real-world residual RL pipeline.
card.key_idea: A policy-agnostic framework that warm-starts tactile encoders/critics using base-policy rollouts, then learns a lightweight tactile residual policy to correct frozen visual motion priors.
card.evaluation: Tested on four contact-rich tasks; improved success rates from 5–40% to 85–100% within 40–80 minutes. Outperformed PLD and ViTAL baselines.
card.limitation: Requires manual resets and risks hardware wear due to repeated contact-rich interactions with fragile tactile sensors.

slides.title: GelNeuro: A Sensing-Computing Integrated Neuromorphic Tactile System for Texture Recognition
slides.highlight: GelNeuro integrates an optical tactile front end with a neuromorphic SoC to achieve high-accuracy texture recognition with significantly lower power consumption than CPU/GPU baselines.

card.one_liner: GelNeuro integrates a visuo-tactile sensor with a neuromorphic SoC for ultra-low-power, direct sensor-to-chip texture recognition.
card.key_idea: Pairs GelSight Mini with Speck2f SoC using a spiking convolutional neural network (SCNN) and a hardware-aware weight clamping strategy to mitigate 8-bit quantization noise.
card.evaluation: Tested on 15 natural textures; achieved 96.3% accuracy within 80ms using 19.6mW power, significantly outperforming CPU/GPU baselines in energy efficiency.
card.limitation: Fixed-point quantization and hardware virtualization cause a precision gap compared to full-precision software simulations.
